what: Closing record of Milestone 4 Phase 4: the one look at the final holdout (block 5, the 23 Milestone 1 events), the descriptive report with block-5 counts, and the Milestone 4 report. The holdout creates no claim and no status, and Milestone 4 is not declared accepted.

later_decisions.words: yes continuewith the closing work and push at the end

regenerated_since_the_closing.why: the owner made the replay tests opt-in on 2026-10-08 ("make the replay tests opt-in"), which turned the report's open item about them into a decision and changed the evidence text of its third acceptance criterion; the report is assembled by code from the committed artifacts and was regenerated

accesses.note: The two runs counted in advance are the whole-suite pass that follows this record and the CI run of the push that carries it; a record cannot be committed after the push it is part of without causing another run.

corrected_on_2026_10_08.why: the numbers above (21 in all, 20 replay accesses, 17 found, 4 counted in advance) counted each CI run as one run of the replay tests; the workflow's matrix runs the whole suite in two jobs and both ran the replay tests in CI runs #232 and #233, so each was four accesses, not two. The accounting record holds the corrected count and the correction.

cross_check.what: docs/M4-PHASE4-RESULTS.md compared with the committed results, the protocol, the logs and the code: the tables row by row by script, the states and counts with the protocol's disclosures, the development comparisons with the Phase 2 and 3 results, the logs with verify_chain and git, the frozen counts with the descriptive report; it read no sealed label file
the_problems: the C1 Brier identity (0.2495 + 0.0046 = 0.2541 should have been 0.2495 + 0.0047 = 0.2543)
the frozen-count comparison was described over 128 events for every target
an account of why C1 scored worst that went further than the arithmetic supports
the independent recomputation was described as covering the M3 fits

verification.replayed_by_a_test: tests/test_m4_phase4_results.py (ReplayTests) runs the look again through Harness.look against temporary logs and compares the outputs with the committed ones, and recomputes scores, contrasts, bootstrap intervals, the C1 to C4 predictions and the M2 fits with plain arithmetic (tests/m4_independent.py)
not_recomputed_independently: the Day-1 return's quantile and ridge predictions (C1 to C3 quantiles, M3 ridge): reproduced by the replay and scored by the independent arithmetic, but never recomputed independently from the training labels, in this or an earlier phase

tests.how: pass 1 ran everything except the replay tests (each run of which is two counted accesses) before this record existed: 988 tests run, only the record's own tests failing at setup; pass 2 runs all 1000, replay tests included, after it

mutation_check.run_on: a snapshot of the committed state (c4a524d), in five runs that shared the list

details_settled_before_the_look: reports/m4-phase4-authorization-2026-10-07.json (P4-1 to P4-14), committed before any Phase 4 code existed
not_done_and_not_authorized: A second look at the holdout other than a technical rerun that does not depend on any holdout result; any selection, tuning, re-run with other settings or change made after a holdout result was seen
Any amendment to the frozen protocol (a new version), any new data or provider, any change to a predictor
Any status, claim or edge statement derived from the holdout (the holdout alone never creates a claim)
Milestone 5 (trees, ensembles) or later, any ranking, candidate list, trading, sizing or backtest modelling
Declaring Milestone 4 accepted (the owner's separate decision)
open_for_the_owner: Whether Milestone 4 is accepted (the protocol makes it the owner's decision)
Whether the replay tests keep running automatically (each run, local or in CI, adds two counted accesses) or only on request; offered with the decision to count them and not chosen
Whether the protocol's criterion 'the holdout was looked at once' is met, given the counted accesses; the report marks it for the owner to judge
The review items still open from the protocol and the protocol-silent details that could move a result (listed in the report under open_for_the_owner); the defaults are in force
not_a_claim: Not a claim of a predictive edge: no status, including DISTINGUISHABLE_BETTER, is one, and none was reached.
Not evidence about any market: a convenience sample of 23 issuers on one regime, and block 5 is entirely Milestone 1 events (time and selection regime are confounded).
